name: Baseten
title: More seller time on technically qualified accounts
subtitle: Enrichment · Provider orchestration · Rep productivity
focus: Connect reliable account data to inference workload context, while reducing duplicate tools, enrichment spend and rep research.
priorities: Build CRM enrichment and account intelligence workflows.
Connect Salesforce, Clay and Harmonic context.
Automate repetitive GTM work and measure rep productivity.
Evaluate stack overlap, data quality and workflow cost.
layers: Company research, product interest and technical workload evidence.
Fill the missing field with the least redundant approved provider.
Keep latency, throughput, deployment constraints and owner attached to the account.
Deliver one useful seller / solutions brief and record whether it helped.
rules: A company building AI is not automatically a qualified inference workload.
Stop enrichment after a verified answer; retain provider and cost.
Ask about deployment constraints instead of inferring confidential infrastructure.

personas.name: ML platform lead
personas.pain: Production serving constraints that generic prospecting misses
personas.promise: A focused technical conversation about the workload and evaluation criteria.
personas.subject: The workload behind {{product}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, before a platform conversation, I’d like to understand the model-serving workload: response pattern, throughput, latency and the constraints your team needs to preserve. Which one currently limits your next rollout?
personas.question: What representative workload would make an evaluation useful?

personas.name: GTM operations
personas.pain: Duplicate tools and enrichment that does not change a seller decision
personas.promise: A measured waterfall that fills only the missing, useful fields.
personas.subject: One useful account brief
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, a seller should not have to reconcile multiple enrichment tools before a call. I’d start with the fields that change qualification, keep the source and cost, and stop when they are verified. Which recurring research task takes the most seller time?
personas.question: Which provider field improves a decision enough to justify its cost?

pitch: I have sold technical products across engineering and business stakeholders, and I now build AI-assisted data and commercial workflows. At BeBop Sensors I led technical sales through validation, proposals and negotiation. At Baseten, I would combine that seller’s judgment with source-backed research, careful enrichment and workload-aware handoffs that save reps time.
mappings: Local CRM with contact provenance, imports and campaign drafts.
Deliver the technical brief where a seller already works.
Hey Sammy: source extraction, model comparisons and workflow cost review.
Compare the whole workflow, including factual quality and recovery.
BeBop: $2.5M development revenue; technical enterprise selling.
Translate deployment and engineering questions into a useful next conversation.
northStar: Seller productivity on qualified inference accounts
weekOne: One sourced workload brief that two sellers and a solutions partner can use.
days60: Expand the provider waterfall and measure quality, tool redundancy, cost and seller adoption.
days90: Connect the strongest research signals to technical evaluation outcomes and refine the stack from measured usefulness.

competitors.name: Modal
competitors.context: Provides serverless inference, sandboxes and training infrastructure.
competitors.question: Which workload constraints favor a serverless compute workflow, dedicated inference support or a self-hosted deployment? Establish throughput, latency, scale and engineering requirements first.

competitors.name: Fireworks
competitors.context: Markets a platform for running, composing and training open models.
competitors.question: Which model, tuning, deployment and operational requirements are decisive for this account? Use a representative benchmark rather than unsupported speed or price claims.

firstBuilds.title: Workload-aware account brief
firstBuilds.goal: Help sellers and solutions teams share the right qualification context.
firstBuilds.scope: 20 accounts with two sellers and a solutions partner.
firstBuilds.measure: Research time, accepted briefs, factual edits and technical meetings held.

firstBuilds.title: Provider waterfall
firstBuilds.goal: Reduce redundant enrichment while preserving useful data quality.
firstBuilds.scope: One field set across a bounded account cohort.
firstBuilds.measure: Verified fields, stale data, tool overlap and cost per useful account.

firstBuilds.title: Rep workflow scorecard
firstBuilds.goal: See whether the automation changes seller work.
firstBuilds.scope: One repeating research task before expanding to more tooling.
firstBuilds.measure: Minutes per account, rep edits, adoption and downstream qualification.

projectRelevance.sammy: Source-grounded extraction and model/tool comparisons are relevant to provider quality, enrichment cost and trustworthy account context.
projectRelevance.sidequest: The partnership CRM demonstrates deduplicated imports and commercial context delivered in a working tool.
projectRelevance.dancers: Recoverable inquiries, signed webhooks and approval flows are patterns for dependable rep workflows and external-tool orchestration.
